#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: ./start.sh <project> [docker compose args...]
#   ./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d
#   ./start.sh my-workspace down
#
# Each project lives in .projects/<project>/ and provides its own .env and agent.yaml.
# The compose file is selected automatically from RUNTIME_PROFILE in the project .env:
#   RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-subprocess (default) → docker-compose.yml
#   RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker              → docker-compose.local-docker.yml
#
# To create a new project:
#   mkdir -p .projects/my-workspace
#   cp .projects/.env.example .projects/my-workspace/.env
#   cp .projects/agent.yaml.example .projects/my-workspace/agent.yaml
#   # Edit both files, then:
#   ./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT="${1:?Usage: ./start.sh <project> [docker compose args...]}"
shift

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/.projects/$PROJECT"

if [[ ! -d "$PROJECT_DIR" ]]; then
  echo "Error: project '$PROJECT' not found (looked in $PROJECT_DIR)"
  echo "Create it with:"
  echo "  mkdir -p .projects/$PROJECT"
  echo "  cp .projects/.env.example .projects/$PROJECT/.env"
  echo "  cp .projects/agent.yaml.example .projects/$PROJECT/agent.yaml"
  exit 1
fi

WORKFLOW_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"

set -a
# 1. Workflow root .env — machine-level local paths shared across all projects.
#    (RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH, GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH, WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH, etc.)
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
[[ -f "$WORKFLOW_ROOT/.env" ]] && source "$WORKFLOW_ROOT/.env"

# 2. Project .env — Docker config (top) and runtime vars (bottom).
#    Project values override anything set in the workflow root .env.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "$PROJECT_DIR/.env"
PROJECT_ENV_FILE="$PROJECT_DIR/.env"
AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH="$PROJECT_DIR/agent.yaml"
set +a

# Select compose file based on RUNTIME_PROFILE.
if [[ "${RUNTIME_PROFILE:-local-subprocess}" == "local-docker" ]]; then
  COMPOSE_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/docker-compose.local-docker.yml"
else
  COMPOSE_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/docker-compose.yml"
fi

exec docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" "$@"

content.content:
1	# Agent Runtime — local-docker Quickstart (M:N topology)
2	
3	Run multiple orchestrators with per-task executor containers and a shared Redis-backed broker.
4	
5	> **New to local deployment?** Start with [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md) (`local-subprocess` — single container, no Redis, easier setup). Switch to `local-docker` when you need:
6	> - Multiple orchestrators sharing work from the same task queue
7	> - Per-task container isolation (executor runs in its own container with its own image)
8	> - The Redis-backed broker topology that matches the production architecture
9	
10	---
11	
12	## How it works
13	
14	```
15	┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
16	│ orchestrator │  │ orchestrator │  │ orchestrator │  ← N agents, each claims tasks
17	│   agent-1    │  │   agent-2    │  │   agent-3    │    via git push race
18	└──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘
19	       │  docker run -d   │                   │
20	       ▼                  ▼                   ▼
21	  ┌─────────┐        ┌─────────┐        ┌─────────┐
22	  │ executor│        │ executor│        │ executor│  ← one container per task
23	  │ for T-x │        │ for T-y │        │ for T-z │
24	  └────┬────┘        └────┬────┘        └────┬────┘
25	       │  POST /callback   │                   │
26	       └──────────────────►│◄──────────────────┘
27	                  ┌────────┴───────┐
28	                  │   broker:7000  │  ← Go broker (T7) + Redis
29	                  └────────────────┘
30	```
31	
32	Each orchestrator spawns executor containers via `docker run -d` on `agents-net`.
33	Runners POST results to the shared broker; **any** orchestrator drains completions
34	opportunistically — the orchestrator that submitted a task is not necessarily the
35	one that handles its result.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Prerequisites
40	
41	Everything from [QUICKSTART.md prerequisites](QUICKSTART.md) plus:
42	
43	- Docker socket accessible at `/var/run/docker.sock` (required for `docker run -d`)
44	- Docker on the host can pull / has access to the executor image (`executor:current`)
45	
46	---
47	
48	## 1. Configure
49	
50	Same project-directory setup as `local-subprocess`:
51	
52	```bash
53	cd runtime/orchestrator/templates
54	
55	mkdir -p .projects/my-workspace
56	cp .projects/.env.example .projects/my-workspace/.env
57	cp .projects/agent.yaml.example .projects/my-workspace/agent.yaml
58	```
59	
60	Edit `.projects/my-workspace/.env` — same required values as `local-subprocess`, plus:
61	
62	```dotenv
63	# Switch to the M:N topology
64	RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker
65	
66	# Broker URL (default is correct when using compose — only override if running broker externally)
67	# BROKER_URL=http://broker:7000
68	
69	# Threaded Slack notifications (optional).
70	# local-docker reuses the broker's Redis service — no separate Redis instance needed.
71	# REDIS_URL defaults to redis://redis:6379 in docker-compose.local-docker.yml.
72	# SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-your-bot-token
73	```
74	
75	`RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker` tells both `start.sh` (which picks `docker-compose.local-docker.yml`)
76	and the orchestrator binary (which loads `DockerRunAdapter` + `HttpBrokerAdapter`).
77	
78	All other values (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`, etc.) are
79	identical to `local-subprocess`.
80	
81	**Threaded Slack in local-docker:** the broker service already starts a Redis container. Set `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and `notifications.slack.channel_id` in `workspace.yaml` — `REDIS_URL` is wired automatically to `redis://redis:6379` by the compose template. No extra Redis setup is required.
82	
83	---
84	
85	## 2. Start
86	
87	```bash
88	# Start agent-1 + broker + Redis + RAG stack
89	./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d
90	```
91	
92	`start.sh` detects `RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker` from your `.env` and automatically
93	uses `docker-compose.local-docker.yml`, which includes `broker` and `redis` as always-on
94	services (no `--profile` flag required).
95	
96	To follow logs:
97	```bash
98	./start.sh my-workspace logs -f orchestrator-1
99	./start.sh my-workspace logs -f broker
100	```
101	
102	---
103	
104	## 3. Verify
105	
106	```bash
107	# All containers running? (should include redis, broker, orchestrator-1, qdrant, rag-server, indexer)
108	./start.sh my-workspace ps
109	
110	# Broker healthy?
111	curl -s http://localhost:7000/health | jq .
112	
113	# Orchestrator using local-docker profile?
114	./start.sh my-workspace logs orchestrator-1 | grep runtime_profile
115	```
116	
117	Expected: broker responds `{"status":"ok"}`; orchestrator logs show `"runtime_profile":"local-docker"`.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## 4. Executor concurrency
122	
123	`orchestrator-1` spawns up to `MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS` executor containers in
124	parallel (default: 4). Each executor runs one task in its own container and
125	posts its result to the broker when done. You do not need multiple orchestrators
126	to run tasks concurrently — the single orchestrator handles the full default
127	concurrency budget.
128	
129	To follow executor activity:
130	```bash
131	# Live executor containers (one per in-progress task):
132	docker ps --filter label=agent-runtime=executor
133	
134	# Broker queue depth:
135	curl -s http://localhost:7000/stats | jq .
136	```
137	
138	---
139	
140	## 5. Stop and reset
141	
142	```bash
143	# Stop all containers (keep volumes):
144	./start.sh my-workspace down
145	
146	# Stop and wipe volumes (full re-clone + Redis flush on next start):
147	./start.sh my-workspace down -v
148	```
149	
150	---
151	
152	## Differences from local-subprocess
153	
154	| | local-subprocess | local-docker |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| Executor runs as | child process inside the agent container | separate `docker run -d` container per task |
157	| Service name | `agent-1`, `agent-2`, `agent-3` | `orchestrator-1` |
158	| Broker | embedded in-process | separate Go service + Redis |
159	| Concurrency | one task at a time per agent container | up to `MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS` (default 4) per orchestrator |
160	| Docker socket | not required | required (mounted into orchestrator container) |
161	| Extra containers | none | `broker`, `redis` + one executor container per active task |
162	| `RUNTIME_PROFILE` | `local-subprocess` (default) | `local-docker` |
163	| Compose file | `docker-compose.yml` | `docker-compose.local-docker.yml` |
164	| Orchestrator image | `orchestrator-bundled` (includes Claude CLI + executor) | `orchestrator` (~500 MB smaller — no bundled Claude CLI) |
165	
166	### Slim orchestrator image
167	
168	`docker-compose.local-docker.yml` already uses `target: orchestrator` — the slim image without a bundled Claude CLI or executor. This is ~500 MB smaller than `orchestrator-bundled` and is correct for `local-docker` mode where the executor runs in its own container. No override needed.
169	
170	---
171	
172	## Common issues
173	
174	| Symptom | Fix |
175	|---|---|
176	| `Cannot connect to Docker daemon` | Docker socket not accessible in orchestrator container — check `/var/run/docker.sock` is mounted (it is by default in compose) |
177	| `broker: connection refused` | `RUNTIME_PROFILE` not set to `local-docker` in `.env` — `start.sh` used `docker-compose.yml` (no broker) instead of `docker-compose.local-docker.yml` |

# Agent Runtime — local-docker Quickstart (M:N topology)

Run multiple orchestrators with per-task executor containers and a shared Redis-backed broker.

> **New to local deployment?** Start with [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md) (`local-subprocess` — single container, no Redis, easier setup). Switch to `local-docker` when you need:
> - Multiple orchestrators sharing work from the same task queue
> - Per-task container isolation (executor runs in its own container with its own image)
> - The Redis-backed broker topology that matches the production architecture

---

## How it works

```
┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
│ orchestrator │  │ orchestrator │  │ orchestrator │  ← N agents, each claims tasks
│   agent-1    │  │   agent-2    │  │   agent-3    │    via git push race
└──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘
       │  docker run -d   │                   │
       ▼                  ▼                   ▼
  ┌─────────┐        ┌─────────┐        ┌─────────┐
  │ executor│        │ executor│        │ executor│  ← one container per task
  │ for T-x │        │ for T-y │        │ for T-z │
  └────┬────┘        └────┬────┘        └────┬────┘
       │  POST /callback   │                   │
       └──────────────────►│◄──────────────────┘
                  ┌────────┴───────┐
                  │   broker:7000  │  ← Go broker (T7) + Redis
                  └────────────────┘
```

Each orchestrator spawns executor containers via `docker run -d` on `agents-net`.
Runners POST results to the shared broker; **any** orchestrator drains completions
opportunistically — the orchestrator that submitted a task is not necessarily the
one that handles its result.

---

## Prerequisites

Everything from [QUICKSTART.md prerequisites](QUICKSTART.md) plus:

- Docker socket accessible at `/var/run/docker.sock` (required for `docker run -d`)
- Docker on the host can pull / has access to the executor image (`executor:current`)

---

## 1. Configure

Same project-directory setup as `local-subprocess`:

```bash
cd runtime/orchestrator/templates

mkdir -p .projects/my-workspace
cp .projects/.env.example .projects/my-workspace/.env
cp .projects/agent.yaml.example .projects/my-workspace/agent.yaml
```

Edit `.projects/my-workspace/.env` — same required values as `local-subprocess`, plus:

```dotenv
# Switch to the M:N topology
RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker

# Broker URL (default is correct when using compose — only override if running broker externally)
# BROKER_URL=http://broker:7000

# Threaded Slack notifications (optional).
# local-docker reuses the broker's Redis service — no separate Redis instance needed.
# REDIS_URL defaults to redis://redis:6379 in docker-compose.local-docker.yml.
# SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-your-bot-token
```

`RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker` tells both `start.sh` (which picks `docker-compose.local-docker.yml`)
and the orchestrator binary (which loads `DockerRunAdapter` + `HttpBrokerAdapter`).

All other values (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`, etc.) are
identical to `local-subprocess`.

**Threaded Slack in local-docker:** the broker service already starts a Redis container. Set `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and `notifications.slack.channel_id` in `workspace.yaml` — `REDIS_URL` is wired automatically to `redis://redis:6379` by the compose template. No extra Redis setup is required.

---

## 2. Start

```bash
# Start agent-1 + broker + Redis + RAG stack
./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d
```

`start.sh` detects `RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker` from your `.env` and automatically
uses `docker-compose.local-docker.yml`, which includes `broker` and `redis` as always-on
services (no `--profile` flag required).

To follow logs:
```bash
./start.sh my-workspace logs -f orchestrator-1
./start.sh my-workspace logs -f broker
```

---

## 3. Verify

```bash
# All containers running? (should include redis, broker, orchestrator-1, qdrant, rag-server, indexer)
./start.sh my-workspace ps

# Broker healthy?
curl -s http://localhost:7000/health | jq .

# Orchestrator using local-docker profile?
./start.sh my-workspace logs orchestrator-1 | grep runtime_profile
```

Expected: broker responds `{"status":"ok"}`; orchestrator logs show `"runtime_profile":"local-docker"`.

---

## 4. Executor concurrency

`orchestrator-1` spawns up to `MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS` executor containers in
parallel (default: 4). Each executor runs one task in its own container and
posts its result to the broker when done. You do not need multiple orchestrators
to run tasks concurrently — the single orchestrator handles the full default
concurrency budget.

To follow executor activity:
```bash
# Live executor containers (one per in-progress task):
docker ps --filter label=agent-runtime=executor

# Broker queue depth:
curl -s http://localhost:7000/stats | jq .
```

---

## 5. Stop and reset

```bash
# Stop all containers (keep volumes):
./start.sh my-workspace down

# Stop and wipe volumes (full re-clone + Redis flush on next start):
./start.sh my-workspace down -v
```

---

## Differences from local-subprocess

| | local-subprocess | local-docker |
|---|---|---|
| Executor runs as | child process inside the agent container | separate `docker run -d` container per task |
| Service name | `agent-1`, `agent-2`, `agent-3` | `orchestrator-1` |
| Broker | embedded in-process | separate Go service + Redis |
| Concurrency | one task at a time per agent container | up to `MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS` (default 4) per orchestrator |
| Docker socket | not required | required (mounted into orchestrator container) |
| Extra containers | none | `broker`, `redis` + one executor container per active task |
| `RUNTIME_PROFILE` | `local-subprocess` (default) | `local-docker` |
| Compose file | `docker-compose.yml` | `docker-compose.local-docker.yml` |
| Orchestrator image | `orchestrator-bundled` (includes Claude CLI + executor) | `orchestrator` (~500 MB smaller — no bundled Claude CLI) |

### Slim orchestrator image

`docker-compose.local-docker.yml` already uses `target: orchestrator` — the slim image without a bundled Claude CLI or executor. This is ~500 MB smaller than `orchestrator-bundled` and is correct for `local-docker` mode where the executor runs in its own container. No override needed.

---

## Common issues

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Cannot connect to Docker daemon` | Docker socket not accessible in orchestrator container — check `/var/run/docker.sock` is mounted (it is by default in compose) |
| `broker: connection refused` | `RUNTIME_PROFILE` not set to `local-docker` in `.env` — `start.sh` used `docker-compose.yml` (no broker) instead of `docker-compose.local-docker.yml` |
| `nonce_mismatch` in broker logs | A runner retried after the nonce was already consumed — harmless; the broker rejects replays by design |
| Executor containers accumulate in `docker ps -a` | Orphan sweep runs every 60s and removes acked containers automatically; call `docker rm` manually for any pre-shutdown orphans |
| `executor_spawn_failed` — image not found | The executor image wasn't built — run `./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d` (the `--build` flag rebuilds the `executor` service which tags `executor:current`) |
| Orchestrator shows `runtime_profile: local-subprocess` despite `.env` | `RUNTIME_PROFILE` not set to `local-docker` — verify with `./start.sh my-workspace logs orchestrator-1 \| grep runtime_profile` |

# Claude executor — fat image (standalone deployment)
#
# When deployed separately from the orchestrator, this image runs only
# the executor entrypoint. For day-1 single-container deployment, the
# orchestrator Dockerfile bundles both binaries.
#
# Build context: workflow/ root
#   docker build -f runtime/executors/claude/Dockerfile .

FROM node:20-bookworm-slim AS builder

WORKDIR /build/runtime/abi
COPY runtime/abi/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY runtime/abi/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/abi/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build

WORKDIR /build/runtime/executors/claude
COPY runtime/executors/claude/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY runtime/executors/claude/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/executors/claude/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build
RUN npm prune --production

FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm AS runtime

ARG GO_VERSION=1.25.0
# TARGETARCH is auto-populated by BuildKit from the host platform (arm64 on Apple Silicon, amd64 on x86).
# Never hardcode this — the wrong arch installs silently but fails at runtime.
ARG TARGETARCH

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl \
    ca-certificates \
    git \
    jq \
    openssh-client \
    tini \
    gnupg \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN curl -fsSL "https://go.dev/dl/go${GO_VERSION}.linux-${TARGETARCH}.tar.gz" \
    -o /tmp/go.tar.gz \
    && tar -C /usr/local -xzf /tmp/go.tar.gz \
    && rm /tmp/go.tar.gz

ENV PATH="/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"
ENV GOPATH="/go"
ENV PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$PATH"

RUN npm install -g yarn pnpm
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/executors/claude
COPY --from=builder /build/runtime/executors/claude/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=builder /build/runtime/executors/claude/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=builder /build/runtime/executors/claude/package.json ./package.json

WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/abi
COPY --from=builder /build/runtime/abi/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=builder /build/runtime/abi/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=builder /build/runtime/abi/package.json ./package.json

RUN useradd -m -u 1001 -s /bin/bash agent \
    && mkdir -p /agent/ssh /home/agent/.ssh \
    && chmod 700 /home/agent/.ssh \
    && chown -R agent:agent /workflow /home/agent

ENV GOPATH="/home/agent/go"
ENV PATH="/home/agent/go/bin:$PATH"

USER agent

# --install nightly skips the GitHub API "latest tag" lookup that 403s in Docker.
RUN curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash \
    && /home/agent/.foundry/bin/foundryup --install nightly
ENV PATH="/home/agent/.foundry/bin:$PATH"

WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/executors/claude

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", "node", "dist/index.js"]

# ── Stage 1: TypeScript builder ───────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-bookworm-slim AS builder

COPY runtime/abi/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY runtime/abi/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/abi/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build

WORKDIR /build/orchestrator
COPY runtime/orchestrator/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY runtime/orchestrator/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/orchestrator/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build
RUN npm prune --production

# ── Stage 2: executor builder ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-bookworm-slim AS executor-builder

WORKDIR /build/runtime/abi
COPY runtime/abi/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY runtime/abi/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/abi/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build

WORKDIR /build/runtime/executors/claude
COPY runtime/executors/claude/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY runtime/executors/claude/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/executors/claude/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build
RUN npm prune --production

WORKDIR /build/runtime/executors/hermes
COPY runtime/executors/hermes/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY runtime/executors/hermes/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/executors/hermes/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build
RUN npm prune --production

# ── Stage 3: orchestrator base ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Node 20 slim — no Python, no Go, no extra package managers.
# Use this target directly when running local-docker profile (executor is a
# separate container; Claude CLI is not needed here).
FROM node:20-bookworm-slim AS orchestrator

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    git \
    jq \
    openssh-client \
    tini \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── Workspace layout ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WORKDIR /workflow

COPY schemas/ ./schemas/

# Orchestrator
WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/orchestrator
COPY --from=builder /build/orchestrator/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=builder /build/orchestrator/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=builder /build/orchestrator/package.json ./package.json

# ABI (shared)
WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/abi
COPY --from=builder /build/abi/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=builder /build/abi/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=builder /build/abi/package.json ./package.json

# Runner wrapper (no build step — plain ESM JS, no runtime deps)
WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/runner-wrapper
COPY runtime/runner-wrapper/runner.js ./

# ── Non-root user ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN useradd -m -u 1001 -s /bin/bash agent \
    && mkdir -p /agent/data /agent/ssh /agent/workflow /home/agent/.ssh \
    && chmod 700 /home/agent/.ssh \
    && chown -R agent:agent /agent /workflow /home/agent

USER agent

ENV AGENT_YAML_PATH="/agent/agent.yaml"
ENV WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH="/agent/workflow"
ENV WORKSPACES_ROOT="/agent/data"

WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/orchestrator

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", "node", "dist/main.js"]

# ── Stage 4: bundled image (local-subprocess default) ────────────────────────
# Extends orchestrator with Claude CLI + executor dist baked in.
# Required for local-subprocess profile (RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-subprocess).
# This is the default target built by docker-compose.yml.
FROM orchestrator AS orchestrator-bundled

USER root

# ── Python 3 (required for agent tasks that run Python-based implementations) ─
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    python3 \
    python3-pip \
    python3-venv \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── Go (required for agent tasks that build Go services) ─────────────────────
# TARGETARCH is auto-populated by BuildKit from the host platform.
# Never hardcode — wrong arch installs silently but fails at runtime.
ARG GO_VERSION=1.25.0
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN curl -fsSL "https://go.dev/dl/go${GO_VERSION}.linux-${TARGETARCH}.tar.gz" \
    -o /tmp/go.tar.gz \
    && tar -C /usr/local -xzf /tmp/go.tar.gz \
    && rm /tmp/go.tar.gz
ENV PATH="/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"

# ── Claude CLI ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

# ── Hermes CLI (NousResearch) — required for hermes executor profile ──────────
# Installs into an isolated venv (PEP 668 — Bookworm blocks system-wide pip).
# Symlinks the entry point to /usr/local/bin so it is on PATH for all users.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git /opt/hermes-agent \
    && python3 -m venv /opt/hermes-venv \
    && /opt/hermes-venv/bin/pip install --no-cache-dir "/opt/hermes-agent[all]" \
    && rm -rf /opt/hermes-agent \
    && ln -sf /opt/hermes-venv/bin/hermes /usr/local/bin/hermes \
    && hermes --version

# ── Package managers (required for JS/TS tasks) ───────────────────────────────
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10.5.2 --activate && corepack prepare yarn@1.22.22 --activate

# Claude executor dist
WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/executors/claude
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/runtime/executors/claude/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/runtime/executors/claude/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/runtime/executors/claude/package.json ./package.json

# Hermes executor dist
WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/executors/hermes
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/runtime/executors/hermes/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/runtime/executors/hermes/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/runtime/executors/hermes/package.json ./package.json

RUN chown -R agent:agent /workflow/runtime/executors/claude /workflow/runtime/executors/hermes

USER agent

# ── Foundry (forge/cast/anvil) — required for Solidity tasks ─────────────────
# --install nightly skips the GitHub API "latest tag" lookup that 403s in Docker.
RUN curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash \
    && /home/agent/.foundry/bin/foundryup --install nightly
ENV PATH="/home/agent/.foundry/bin:$PATH"

# Smoke-test: HERMES_HOME tmpdir creation works as agent user.
# HERMES_HOME is set at runtime to ${EXECUTOR_WORKDIR}/hermes-home (per-handle tmpdir).
RUN HERMES_TEST_HOME="$(mktemp -d)" \
    && mkdir -p "${HERMES_TEST_HOME}/hermes-home" \
    && rm -rf "${HERMES_TEST_HOME}"

WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/orchestrator

# Agent runtime — local-docker mode (decoupled dispatcher topology)
#
# Decoupled data flow (mirrors prod):
#
#   orchestrator ──XADD──► dispatch-stream (Redis)
#                                │
#                         XREADGROUP │ XAUTOCLAIM
#                                ▼
#                          dispatcher ──docker run──► executor (ephemeral)
#                                │                        │
#                                │              runner wrapper POSTs /callback
#                                │                        │
#                                ▼                        ▼
#                  broker:7000 (Go + Redis) ◄─────────────┘
#                          │
#              listCompleted() │
#                          ▼
#                    orchestrator (drains, advances FSM)
#
# The orchestrator is UNPRIVILEGED — it has no Docker socket and holds no
# credentials. It only enqueues credential-free DispatchJobs to the dispatch
# Redis Stream. The dispatcher holds the Docker socket + credentials and spawns
# executor containers. Executors log to stdout (LOG_SINK=none); no management-repo
# git flush on this path.
#
# For the simpler bundled setup where orchestrator + executor share one container,
# use docker-compose.yml (local-subprocess). start.sh selects the right file
# from RUNTIME_PROFILE in your project .env.
#
# Concurrent-coexistence profile (--profile concurrent-bundled):
#   Starts a second orchestrator in local-subprocess mode alongside the standalone
#   one. Both claim tasks via the same git push race (no contention), but execute
#   via different mechanisms (queue dispatch vs. subprocess). Distinct named
#   volumes isolate their WORKSPACES_ROOT. Designed for T7 coexistence testing.
#
# Required values:
#   .env (Docker section)   → PLATFORM_BIN_DIR, RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker
#   .env (Runtime section)  → GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL
# start.sh sources workflow root .env then project .env.
#
# Usage (via start.sh — recommended):
#   ./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d
#
# Direct usage:
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.local-docker.yml up --build
#   PLATFORM_BIN_DIR=/absolute/path/to/workflow/runtime/runner-wrapper \
#     docker compose -f docker-compose.local-docker.yml up --build

name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-agent-runtime-local}

# ── Shared orchestrator definition (local-docker, unprivileged) ───────────────
x-orchestrator: &orchestrator-base
  build:
    # Build context is workflow/ root so schemas/ is included.
    # Path is two levels up: templates/ → orchestrator/ → runtime/ → workflow/
    context: ../../..
    dockerfile: runtime/orchestrator/Dockerfile
    # Slim orchestrator image — no Claude CLI or executor baked in.
    # In local-docker mode executors run in their own containers; the
    # orchestrator only needs the scheduler binary.
    target: orchestrator
  env_file:
    - path: ${PROJECT_ENV_FILE:-.env}
      required: false
  environment:
    # Hardcoded container paths — never set in .env.
    AGENT_YAML_PATH: /agent/agent.yaml
    WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH: /agent/workflow
    WORKSPACES_ROOT: /agent/data
    RUNTIME_PROFILE: local-docker
    # MAX_TURNS — executor turn budget (default: 200).
    MAX_TURNS: "${MAX_TURNS:-200}"
    # Container-internal defaults — override in .env only if using an external stack.
    MCP_RAG_URL: "${MCP_RAG_URL:-http://rag-server:8000}"
    GITNEXUS_MCP_URL: "${GITNEXUS_MCP_URL:-}"
    BROKER_URL: "${BROKER_URL:-http://broker:7000}"
    # Slack notifications (optional). Reuse broker's redis at redis://redis:6379.
    SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:-}"
    REDIS_URL: "${REDIS_URL:-redis://redis:6379}"
    # All other vars (GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, GIT_AUTHOR_*, REVIEWER_*, etc.)
    # are loaded from the project .env via env_file above.
  volumes:
    - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
    - workflow:/agent/workflow
    # NO Docker socket — the orchestrator is unprivileged on this path.
    # Spawn privilege lives in the dispatcher service.
  networks:
    - agents-net
  depends_on:
    - broker
  restart: unless-stopped
  deploy:
    resources:
      limits:
        cpus: "2"
        memory: 4G
      reservations:
        cpus: "0.5"
        memory: 512M

# ── Shared RAG build context ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
x-rag-build: &rag-build
  context: ${RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH:?Set RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
    of your rag-service clone}
  dockerfile: Dockerfile


# ── Services ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
services:

  # ── Redis ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shared backing store for the Go broker (completion queue) and the dispatch
  # stream (platform:dispatch) owned by the dispatcher consumer group.
  # AOF disabled for dev convenience.
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    networks:
      - agents-net
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 512M
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 64M

  # ── Broker ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Go completion broker. Executors POST results here via runner wrapper;
  # any orchestrator drains completions and updates task state (M:N drain).
  # Also exposes GET /registry-size — the dispatcher reads this to enforce
  # the global spawn cap without an in-process counter.
  # Reachable inside agents-net: http://broker:7000
  broker:
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/broker/Dockerfile
    environment:
      BROKER_ADDR: ":7000"
      REDIS_URL: "redis://redis:6379"
      RECLAIM_INTERVAL: "${BROKER_RECLAIM_INTERVAL:-2}"
    depends_on:
      - redis
    networks:
      - agents-net
    ports:
      - "${BROKER_PORT:-7000}:7000"
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 256M
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 32M

  # ── Dispatcher ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Owns the dispatch Redis Stream (platform:dispatch).
  # Consumes DispatchJobs via XREADGROUP; redelivers stuck entries via XAUTOCLAIM;
  # routes to DLQ after DISPATCHER_MAX_DELIVERIES failed attempts (posting a
  # synthetic "failed" completion to the broker so the orchestrator learns via
  # the normal completion path).
  #
  # Sole holder of spawn privilege: the Docker socket and credentials live here.
  # Per-handle spawn lock (SET NX PX) prevents double-spawn across M:N instances.
  # Global spawn cap enforced via GET /registry-size on the broker.
  #
  # PLATFORM_BIN_DIR must be an ABSOLUTE HOST path to runtime/runner-wrapper/.
  # The dispatcher passes it to `docker run -v PLATFORM_BIN_DIR:/platform:ro`
  # so spawned executor containers find runner.js at /platform/runner.js.
  # Docker interprets the path on the HOST — not inside this container.
  # Set PLATFORM_BIN_DIR in your project .env (absolute path, no ~).
  #
  # WORKSPACES_DIR is similarly a HOST path. Docker creates per-handle
  # subdirectories (exec-<handle>/) automatically on first spawn.
  dispatcher:
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/dispatcher/Dockerfile
    env_file:
      - path: ${PROJECT_ENV_FILE:-.env}
        required: false
    environment:
      REDIS_URL: "redis://redis:6379"
      BROKER_URL: "http://broker:7000"
      # HOST path to runtime/runner-wrapper/ — passed verbatim to `docker run -v`.
      # Must be absolute; Docker daemon (on host) resolves this path.
      PLATFORM_BIN_DIR: "${PLATFORM_BIN_DIR:?Set PLATFORM_BIN_DIR to the absolute host path of runtime/runner-wrapper}"
      # HOST path for per-handle workspace dirs. Default: /tmp/agent-workspaces.
      # Docker creates exec-<handle>/ subdirs here automatically on spawn.
      WORKSPACES_DIR: "${DISPATCHER_WORKSPACES_HOST_PATH:-/tmp/agent-workspaces}"
      EXECUTOR_IMAGE: "${EXECUTOR_IMAGE:-executor:current}"
      # Network name for spawned executor containers.
      # Must match the compose-project-scoped network: {COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_agents-net.
      DOCKER_NETWORK: "${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-agent-runtime-local}_agents-net"
      DISPATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT: "${DISPATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT:-5}"
      DISPATCHER_MAX_DELIVERIES: "${DISPATCHER_MAX_DELIVERIES:-5}"
      DISPATCHER_SPAWN_LOCK_TTL_MS: "${DISPATCHER_SPAWN_LOCK_TTL_MS:-300000}"
      DISPATCHER_POLL_BLOCK_MS: "${DISPATCHER_POLL_BLOCK_MS:-5000}"
      DISPATCHER_XAUTOCLAIM_MIN_IDLE_MS: "${DISPATCHER_XAUTOCLAIM_MIN_IDLE_MS:-30000}"
      DISPATCHER_BATCH_SIZE: "${DISPATCHER_BATCH_SIZE:-10}"
      # Credentials injected into spawned executor containers at runtime.
      # Loaded from project .env via env_file above.
      # GITHUB_TOKEN and SSH_PRIVATE_KEY are picked up automatically.
    volumes:
      # Docker socket — the dispatcher is the sole spawn-privilege holder.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - broker
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 512M
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 64M

  # ── Orchestrator (standalone, local-docker) ───────────────────────────────────
  # Polls workspace(s), claims tasks, registers handles with the broker, and
  # enqueues credential-free DispatchJobs to the dispatch Redis Stream.
  # No Docker socket — no spawn privilege.
  orchestrator-1:
    <<: *orchestrator-base
    volumes:
      - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
      - workspaces-orchestrator1:/agent/data
      - workflow:/agent/workflow
      # NO Docker socket — orchestrator is unprivileged on the local-docker path.

  # ── Concurrent-coexistence orchestrator (bundled, local-subprocess) ───────────
  # Enabled with: --profile concurrent-bundled
  # Runs a BUNDLED (local-subprocess) orchestrator alongside orchestrator-1.
  # Both orchestrators may claim tasks from the same workspace via the git push
  # race — no contention; the claim protocol is atomic. The bundled orchestrator
  # executes tasks as child subprocesses (LOG_SINK=git, git flush active);
  # the standalone orchestrator dispatches via the Redis stream (LOG_SINK=none).
  # Distinct WORKSPACES_ROOT volumes prevent workspace-dir collisions.
  # Designed for T7 concurrent-coexistence verification.
  orchestrator-bundled:
    profiles:
      - concurrent-bundled
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/orchestrator/Dockerfile
      # Bundled image includes Claude CLI + executor — required for local-subprocess.
      target: orchestrator-bundled
    env_file:
      - path: ${PROJECT_ENV_FILE:-.env}
        required: false
    environment:
      AGENT_YAML_PATH: /agent/agent.yaml
      WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH: /agent/workflow
      WORKSPACES_ROOT: /agent/data
      # Bundled path: executors run as child subprocesses; no dispatcher needed.
      RUNTIME_PROFILE: local-subprocess
      MAX_TURNS: "${MAX_TURNS:-200}"
      MCP_RAG_URL: "${MCP_RAG_URL:-http://rag-server:8000}"
      GITNEXUS_MCP_URL: "${GITNEXUS_MCP_URL:-}"
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:-}"
      REDIS_URL: "${REDIS_URL:-redis://redis:6379}"
    volumes:
      - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
      # Separate volume — isolates WORKSPACES_ROOT from orchestrator-1.
      - workspaces-orchestrator-bundled:/agent/data
      - workflow:/agent/workflow
      # Docker socket harmless (unused) in local-subprocess mode.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "4"
          memory: 10G
        reservations:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 2G

  # ── Executor image ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Build-only service — tags executor:current on the host so the dispatcher
  # can `docker run -d executor:current` per task without a separate build step.
  # The container exits immediately; the image stays on the host.
  executor:
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/executors/claude/Dockerfile
    image: executor:current
    entrypoint: ["true"]
    restart: "no"

  # ── RAG stack ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # All RAG services join agents-net so orchestrator and executor containers
  # resolve rag-server:8000 by service-name DNS.
  qdrant:
    image: qdrant/qdrant:latest
    ports:
      - "${QDRANT_PORT:-6333}:6333"
      - "${QDRANT_GRPC_PORT:-6334}:6334"
    volumes:
      - qdrant_data:/qdrant/storage
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.25"
          memory: 256M

  rag-server:
    build: *rag-build
    command: [ "python", "-m", "services.rag_server.main" ]
    depends_on:
      - qdrant
    ports:
      - "${RAG_SERVER_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      QDRANT_URL: "${QDRANT_URL:-http://qdrant:6333}"
      WORKSPACE_ID: "${WORKSPACE_ID:?WORKSPACE_ID must be set — e.g. 'workspace'}"
      NO_PROXY: "*"
      no_proxy: "*"
      HF_HUB_OFFLINE: "1"
      TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE: "1"
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 1G

  indexer:
    build: *rag-build
    command: [ "python", "-m", "services.indexer.main" ]
    depends_on:
      - qdrant
    environment:
      QDRANT_URL: "${QDRANT_URL:-http://qdrant:6333}"
      WORKSPACE_ID: "${WORKSPACE_ID:?WORKSPACE_ID must be set — e.g. 'workspace'}"
      INDEXER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS: "${INDEXER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS:-300}"
      WORKSPACE_YAML_PATH: /workspace/workspace.yaml
      SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY}"
      GITHUB_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"
      PR_INDEX_STATE_PATH: "/app/pr_index_state/state.json"
      NO_PROXY: "*"
      no_proxy: "*"
    volumes:
      - ${WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH:?Set WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH to your local
        workspace clone path}/workspace.yaml:/workspace/workspace.yaml:ro
      - pr_index_state:/app/pr_index_state
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 1G

  # ── GitNexus stack (optional) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Set GITNEXUS_MCP_URL=http://gitnexus-server:8002 in .env to enable.
  gitnexus-indexer:
    build:
      context: ${GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH:?Set GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
        of your git-nexus clone}/services/gitnexus_indexer
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      WORKSPACE_URL: "${WORKSPACE_URL:?WORKSPACE_URL must be set — SSH URL of the workspace management repo}"
      SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
      GITNEXUS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS: "${GITNEXUS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS:-300}"
      HOME: /gitnexus-data
    volumes:
      - gitnexus-data:/gitnexus-data
    networks:

    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:

        reservations:
          cpus: "0.25"
          memory: 512M

    build:
      context: ${GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH:?Set GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
        of your git-nexus clone}/services/gitnexus_server
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      HOME: /gitnexus-data
      GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRIES: "${GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRIES:-10}"

    # Bridge network shared by the orchestrator, dispatcher, dynamically-spawned

    # In local-docker mode executors run in their own containers; the
    # orchestrator only needs the scheduler binary.
    target: orchestrator
  env_file:
    - path: ${PROJECT_ENV_FILE:-.env}
      required: false
  environment:
    # Hardcoded container paths — never set in .env.
    AGENT_YAML_PATH: /agent/agent.yaml
    WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH: /agent/workflow
    WORKSPACES_ROOT: /agent/data
    RUNTIME_PROFILE: local-docker
    # MAX_TURNS — executor turn budget (default: 200).
    MAX_TURNS: "${MAX_TURNS:-200}"
    # Container-internal defaults — override in .env only if using an external stack.
    MCP_RAG_URL: "${MCP_RAG_URL:-http://rag-server:8000}"
    GITNEXUS_MCP_URL: "${GITNEXUS_MCP_URL:-}"
    BROKER_URL: "${BROKER_URL:-http://broker:7000}"
    # Slack notifications (optional). Reuse broker's redis at redis://redis:6379.
    SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:-}"
    REDIS_URL: "${REDIS_URL:-redis://redis:6379}"
    # All other vars (GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, GIT_AUTHOR_*, REVIEWER_*, etc.)
    # are loaded from the project .env via env_file above.
  volumes:
    - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
    - workflow:/agent/workflow
    # NO Docker socket — the orchestrator is unprivileged on this path.
    # Spawn privilege lives in the dispatcher service.
  networks:
    - agents-net
  depends_on:
    - broker
  restart: unless-stopped
  deploy:
    resources:
      limits:
        cpus: "2"
        memory: 4G
      reservations:
        cpus: "0.5"
        memory: 512M

# ── Shared RAG build context ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
x-rag-build: &rag-build
  context: ${RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH:?Set RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
    of your rag-service clone}
  dockerfile: Dockerfile


# ── Services ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
services:

  # ── Redis ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shared backing store for the Go broker (completion queue) and the dispatch
  # stream (platform:dispatch) owned by the dispatcher consumer group.
  # AOF disabled for dev convenience.
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    networks:
      - agents-net
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 512M
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 64M

  # ── Broker ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Go completion broker. Executors POST results here via runner wrapper;
  # any orchestrator drains completions and updates task state (M:N drain).
  # Also exposes GET /registry-size — the dispatcher reads this to enforce
  # the global spawn cap without an in-process counter.
  # Reachable inside agents-net: http://broker:7000
  broker:
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/broker/Dockerfile
    environment:
      BROKER_ADDR: ":7000"
      REDIS_URL: "redis://redis:6379"
      RECLAIM_INTERVAL: "${BROKER_RECLAIM_INTERVAL:-2}"
    depends_on:
      - redis
    networks:
      - agents-net
    ports:
      - "${BROKER_PORT:-7000}:7000"
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 256M
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 32M

  # ── Dispatcher ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Owns the dispatch Redis Stream (platform:dispatch).
  # Consumes DispatchJobs via XREADGROUP; redelivers stuck entries via XAUTOCLAIM;
  # routes to DLQ after DISPATCHER_MAX_DELIVERIES failed attempts (posting a
  # synthetic "failed" completion to the broker so the orchestrator learns via
  # the normal completion path).
  #
  # Sole holder of spawn privilege: the Docker socket and credentials live here.
  # Per-handle spawn lock (SET NX PX) prevents double-spawn across M:N instances.
  # Global spawn cap enforced via GET /registry-size on the broker.
  #
  # PLATFORM_BIN_DIR must be an ABSOLUTE HOST path to runtime/runner-wrapper/.
  # The dispatcher passes it to `docker run -v PLATFORM_BIN_DIR:/platform:ro`
  # so spawned executor containers find runner.js at /platform/runner.js.
  # Docker interprets the path on the HOST — not inside this container.
  # Set PLATFORM_BIN_DIR in your project .env (absolute path, no ~).
  #
  # WORKSPACES_DIR is similarly a HOST path. Docker creates per-handle
  # subdirectories (exec-<handle>/) automatically on first spawn.
  dispatcher:
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/dispatcher/Dockerfile
    env_file:
      - path: ${PROJECT_ENV_FILE:-.env}
        required: false
    environment:
      REDIS_URL: "redis://redis:6379"
      BROKER_URL: "http://broker:7000"
      # HOST path to runtime/runner-wrapper/ — passed verbatim to `docker run -v`.
      # Must be absolute; Docker daemon (on host) resolves this path.
      PLATFORM_BIN_DIR: "${PLATFORM_BIN_DIR:?Set PLATFORM_BIN_DIR to the absolute host path of runtime/runner-wrapper}"
      # HOST path for per-handle workspace dirs. Default: /tmp/agent-workspaces.
      # Docker creates exec-<handle>/ subdirs here automatically on spawn.
      WORKSPACES_DIR: "${DISPATCHER_WORKSPACES_HOST_PATH:-/tmp/agent-workspaces}"
      EXECUTOR_IMAGE: "${EXECUTOR_IMAGE:-executor:current}"
      # Network name for spawned executor containers.
      # Must match the compose-project-scoped network: {COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_agents-net.
      DOCKER_NETWORK: "${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-agent-runtime-local}_agents-net"
      DISPATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT: "${DISPATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT:-5}"
      DISPATCHER_MAX_DELIVERIES: "${DISPATCHER_MAX_DELIVERIES:-5}"
      DISPATCHER_SPAWN_LOCK_TTL_MS: "${DISPATCHER_SPAWN_LOCK_TTL_MS:-300000}"
      DISPATCHER_POLL_BLOCK_MS: "${DISPATCHER_POLL_BLOCK_MS:-5000}"
      DISPATCHER_XAUTOCLAIM_MIN_IDLE_MS: "${DISPATCHER_XAUTOCLAIM_MIN_IDLE_MS:-30000}"
      DISPATCHER_BATCH_SIZE: "${DISPATCHER_BATCH_SIZE:-10}"
      # Credentials injected into spawned executor containers at runtime.
      # Loaded from project .env via env_file above.
      # GITHUB_TOKEN and SSH_PRIVATE_KEY are picked up automatically.
    volumes:
      # Docker socket — the dispatcher is the sole spawn-privilege holder.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - broker
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 512M
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 64M

  # ── Orchestrator (standalone, local-docker) ───────────────────────────────────
  # Polls workspace(s), claims tasks, registers handles with the broker, and
  # enqueues credential-free DispatchJobs to the dispatch Redis Stream.
  # No Docker socket — no spawn privilege.
  orchestrator-1:
    <<: *orchestrator-base
    volumes:
      - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
      - workspaces-orchestrator1:/agent/data
      - workflow:/agent/workflow
      # NO Docker socket — orchestrator is unprivileged on the local-docker path.

  # ── Concurrent-coexistence orchestrator (bundled, local-subprocess) ───────────
  # Enabled with: --profile concurrent-bundled
  # Runs a BUNDLED (local-subprocess) orchestrator alongside orchestrator-1.
  # Both orchestrators may claim tasks from the same workspace via the git push
  # race — no contention; the claim protocol is atomic. The bundled orchestrator
  # executes tasks as child subprocesses (LOG_SINK=git, git flush active);
  # the standalone orchestrator dispatches via the Redis stream (LOG_SINK=none).
  # Distinct WORKSPACES_ROOT volumes prevent workspace-dir collisions.
  # Designed for T7 concurrent-coexistence verification.
  orchestrator-bundled:
    profiles:
      - concurrent-bundled
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/orchestrator/Dockerfile
      # Bundled image includes Claude CLI + executor — required for local-subprocess.
      target: orchestrator-bundled
    env_file:
      - path: ${PROJECT_ENV_FILE:-.env}
        required: false
    environment:
      AGENT_YAML_PATH: /agent/agent.yaml
      WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH: /agent/workflow
      WORKSPACES_ROOT: /agent/data
      # Bundled path: executors run as child subprocesses; no dispatcher needed.
      RUNTIME_PROFILE: local-subprocess
      MAX_TURNS: "${MAX_TURNS:-200}"
      MCP_RAG_URL: "${MCP_RAG_URL:-http://rag-server:8000}"
      GITNEXUS_MCP_URL: "${GITNEXUS_MCP_URL:-}"
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:-}"
      REDIS_URL: "${REDIS_URL:-redis://redis:6379}"
    volumes:
      - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
      # Separate volume — isolates WORKSPACES_ROOT from orchestrator-1.
      - workspaces-orchestrator-bundled:/agent/data
      - workflow:/agent/workflow
      # Docker socket harmless (unused) in local-subprocess mode.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "4"
          memory: 10G
        reservations:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 2G

  # ── Executor image ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Build-only service — tags executor:current on the host so the dispatcher
  # can `docker run -d executor:current` per task without a separate build step.
  # The container exits immediately; the image stays on the host.
  executor:
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/executors/claude/Dockerfile
    image: executor:current
    entrypoint: ["true"]
    restart: "no"

  # ── RAG stack ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # All RAG services join agents-net so orchestrator and executor containers
  # resolve rag-server:8000 by service-name DNS.
  qdrant:
    image: qdrant/qdrant:latest
    ports:
      - "${QDRANT_PORT:-6333}:6333"
      - "${QDRANT_GRPC_PORT:-6334}:6334"
    volumes:
      - qdrant_data:/qdrant/storage
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.25"
          memory: 256M

  rag-server:
    build: *rag-build
    command: [ "python", "-m", "services.rag_server.main" ]
    depends_on:
      - qdrant
    ports:
      - "${RAG_SERVER_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      QDRANT_URL: "${QDRANT_URL:-http://qdrant:6333}"
      WORKSPACE_ID: "${WORKSPACE_ID:?WORKSPACE_ID must be set — e.g. 'workspace'}"
      NO_PROXY: "*"
      no_proxy: "*"
      HF_HUB_OFFLINE: "1"
      TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE: "1"
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 1G

  indexer:
    build: *rag-build
    command: [ "python", "-m", "services.indexer.main" ]
    depends_on:
      - qdrant
    environment:
      QDRANT_URL: "${QDRANT_URL:-http://qdrant:6333}"
      WORKSPACE_ID: "${WORKSPACE_ID:?WORKSPACE_ID must be set — e.g. 'workspace'}"
      INDEXER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS: "${INDEXER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS:-300}"
      WORKSPACE_YAML_PATH: /workspace/workspace.yaml
      SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY}"
      GITHUB_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"
      PR_INDEX_STATE_PATH: "/app/pr_index_state/state.json"
      NO_PROXY: "*"
      no_proxy: "*"
    volumes:
      - ${WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH:?Set WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH to your local
        workspace clone path}/workspace.yaml:/workspace/workspace.yaml:ro
      - pr_index_state:/app/pr_index_state
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 1G

  # ── GitNexus stack (optional) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Set GITNEXUS_MCP_URL=http://gitnexus-server:8002 in .env to enable.
  gitnexus-indexer:
    build:
      context: ${GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH:?Set GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
        of your git-nexus clone}/services/gitnexus_indexer
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      WORKSPACE_URL: "${WORKSPACE_URL:?WORKSPACE_URL must be set — SSH URL of the workspace management repo}"
      SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
      GITNEXUS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS: "${GITNEXUS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS:-300}"
      HOME: /gitnexus-data
    volumes:
      - gitnexus-data:/gitnexus-data
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.25"
          memory: 512M

  gitnexus-server:
    build:
      context: ${GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH:?Set GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
        of your git-nexus clone}/services/gitnexus_server
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      HOME: /gitnexus-data
      GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRIES: "${GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRIES:-10}"
      GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRY_DELAY: "${GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRY_DELAY:-5.0}"
    ports:
      - "${GITNEXUS_SERVER_PORT:-8002}:8002"
    volumes:
      - gitnexus-data:/gitnexus-data
    depends_on:
      - gitnexus-indexer
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 1G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 128M

# ── Networks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
networks:
  agents-net:
    # Bridge network shared by the orchestrator, dispatcher, dynamically-spawned
    # executor containers, broker, Redis, and the RAG stack.
    # Executor containers join via --network {COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_agents-net
    # (set in DOCKER_NETWORK env of the dispatcher service).
    driver: bridge

# ── Volumes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
volumes:
  workspaces-orchestrator1:
    driver: local
  # Isolated WORKSPACES_ROOT for the concurrent-bundled orchestrator.
  # Used only when --profile concurrent-bundled is active (T7 coexistence tests).
  workspaces-orchestrator-bundled:
    driver: local
  workflow:
    driver: local
  redis_data:
    driver: local
  qdrant_data:
    driver: local
  # PR index cursor state — scoped per project by COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME prefix.
  pr_index_state:
    driver: local
  gitnexus-data:
    driver: local

# Agent runtime — local-docker mode (core services)
#
# Contains per-workspace core services: orchestrator, executor, broker, Redis,
# and the optional RAG + GitNexus stacks. Run one stack per workspace.
#
# End-user-facing services (digital-factory-ui, api-service, adapter-service,
# PostgreSQL, workspace Redis) live in docker-compose.platform.yml (repo root).
# Start that file once — it is shared across all workspace stacks.
#
# Topology: one orchestrator + up to N executor containers (default cap: 4).
#
#   orchestrator-1  →  docker run -d executor:current  (per task, on-demand)
#         │                        │
#         │              runner wrapper POSTs /callback on exit
#         │                        │
#         │                        ▼
#         └── listCompleted() ◄─ broker:7000  (Go broker + Redis)
#
# The orchestrator is a lightweight scheduler — it claims tasks via git push
# race and spawns executor containers via DockerRunAdapter. A runner wrapper
# exec's the executor binary; on exit it POSTs the result to the broker. The
# orchestrator drains completions via listCompleted() and updates task state.
#
# Executors are ephemeral: one container per task, reaped after completion.
# They are NOT long-running compose services — the orchestrator spawns them
# dynamically. The `executor` service below exists only to build the image;
# it exits immediately and the image stays on the host for `docker run -d`.
#
# For the simpler single-container setup where orchestrator and executor share
# one container, use docker-compose.yml (local-subprocess) instead.
# start.sh selects the right file from RUNTIME_PROFILE in your project .env.
#
# Required values:
#   .env (Docker section)   → RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH, WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH, WORKSPACE_ID, RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker
#   .env (Runtime section)  → GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME / GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL
# start.sh sources workflow root .env then project .env.
#
# Usage (via start.sh — recommended):
#   ./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d
#
# Direct usage:
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.local-docker.yml up --build

name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-agent-runtime-local}

# ── Shared orchestrator definition ───────────────────────────────────────────
x-orchestrator: &orchestrator-base
  build:
    # Build context is workflow/ root so schemas/ is included.
    # Path is two levels up: templates/ → orchestrator/ → runtime/ → workflow/
    context: ../../..
    dockerfile: runtime/orchestrator/Dockerfile
    # Slim orchestrator image — no Claude CLI or executor baked in.
    # In local-docker mode executors run in their own containers, so the
    # orchestrator only needs the scheduler binary.
    target: orchestrator
  env_file:
    - path: ${PROJECT_ENV_FILE:-.env}
      required: false
  environment:
    # Hardcoded container paths — never set in .env.
    AGENT_YAML_PATH: /agent/agent.yaml
    WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH: /agent/workflow
    WORKSPACES_ROOT: /agent/data
    RUNTIME_PROFILE: local-docker
    # MAX_TURNS — executor turn budget (default: 200). Inherited by all executor
    # subprocesses via the orchestrator's process environment.
    MAX_TURNS: "${MAX_TURNS:-200}"
    # Container-internal defaults — override in .env only if using an external stack.
    MCP_RAG_URL: "${MCP_RAG_URL:-http://rag-server:8000}"
    GITNEXUS_MCP_URL: "${GITNEXUS_MCP_URL:-}"
    BROKER_URL: "${BROKER_URL:-http://broker:7000}"
    # Threaded Slack notifications (optional). Set SLACK_BOT_TOKEN to enable.
    # local-docker: the broker's Redis service is reused at redis://redis:6379.
    SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:-}"
    REDIS_URL: "${REDIS_URL:-redis://redis:6379}"
    # All other vars (GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, GIT_AUTHOR_*, REVIEWER_*, etc.)
    # are loaded from the project .env via env_file above.
  volumes:
    - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
    - workflow:/agent/workflow
    # Docker socket — required for DockerRunAdapter (spawns executor containers).
    - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
  networks:
    - agents-net
  depends_on:
    - broker
  restart: unless-stopped
  deploy:
    resources:
      limits:
        cpus: "2"
        memory: 4G
      reservations:
        cpus: "0.5"
        memory: 512M

# ── Shared RAG build context ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
x-rag-build: &rag-build
  context: ${RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH:?Set RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
    of your rag-service clone}
  dockerfile: Dockerfile


# ── Services ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
services:

  # ── Redis ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Backing store for the Go broker. AOF disabled for dev convenience.
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    networks:
      - agents-net
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 512M
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 64M

  # ── Broker ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Go completion broker. The orchestrator registers a handle per spawned
  # executor; executors POST their result here when done; the orchestrator
  # drains completions and updates task state.
  # Reachable by service-name DNS inside agents-net: http://broker:7000
  broker:
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/broker/Dockerfile
    environment:
      BROKER_ADDR: ":7000"
      REDIS_URL: "redis://redis:6379"
      RECLAIM_INTERVAL: "${BROKER_RECLAIM_INTERVAL:-2}"
    depends_on:
      - redis
    networks:
      - agents-net
    ports:
      - "${BROKER_PORT:-7000}:7000"
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 256M
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 32M

  # ── Orchestrator ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Single orchestrator — polls workspace(s), claims tasks via git push race,
  # and spawns up to MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS executor containers (default: 4).
  # One orchestrator is sufficient for local-docker mode; add a second only if
  # you are running multiple isolated workspaces that need parallel claiming.
  orchestrator-1:
    <<: *orchestrator-base
    volumes:
      - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
      - workspaces-orchestrator1:/agent/data
      - workflow:/agent/workflow
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

  # ── Executor image ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Build-only service — tags executor:current on the host so the orchestrator
  # can `docker run -d executor:current` per task without a separate build step.
  # The container exits immediately after start; the image stays on the host.
  executor:
    build:
      context: ../../..
      dockerfile: runtime/executors/claude/Dockerfile
    image: executor:current
    entrypoint: ["true"]
    restart: "no"

  # ── RAG stack ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # All RAG services join agents-net so the orchestrator and executor containers
  # resolve rag-server:8000 by service-name DNS.
  qdrant:
    image: qdrant/qdrant:latest
    ports:
      - "${QDRANT_PORT:-6333}:6333"
      - "${QDRANT_GRPC_PORT:-6334}:6334"
    volumes:
      - qdrant_data:/qdrant/storage
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.25"
          memory: 256M

  rag-server:
    build: *rag-build
    command: [ "python", "-m", "services.rag_server.main" ]
    depends_on:
      - qdrant
    ports:
      - "${RAG_SERVER_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      QDRANT_URL: "${QDRANT_URL:-http://qdrant:6333}"
      WORKSPACE_ID: "${WORKSPACE_ID:?WORKSPACE_ID must be set — e.g. 'workspace'}"
      NO_PROXY: "*"
      no_proxy: "*"
      HF_HUB_OFFLINE: "1"
      TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE: "1"
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 1G

  indexer:
    build: *rag-build
    command: [ "python", "-m", "services.indexer.main" ]
    depends_on:
      - qdrant
    environment:
      QDRANT_URL: "${QDRANT_URL:-http://qdrant:6333}"
      WORKSPACE_ID: "${WORKSPACE_ID:?WORKSPACE_ID must be set — e.g. 'workspace'}"
      INDEXER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS: "${INDEXER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS:-300}"
      WORKSPACE_YAML_PATH: /workspace/workspace.yaml
      SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY}"
      GITHUB_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"
      PR_INDEX_STATE_PATH: "/app/pr_index_state/state.json"
      NO_PROXY: "*"
      no_proxy: "*"
    volumes:
      - ${WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH:?Set WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH to your local
        workspace clone path}/workspace.yaml:/workspace/workspace.yaml:ro
      - pr_index_state:/app/pr_index_state
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: 1G

  # ── GitNexus stack (optional) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Set GITNEXUS_MCP_URL=http://gitnexus-server:8002 in .env to enable.
  gitnexus-indexer:
    build:
      context: ${GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH:?Set GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
        of your git-nexus clone}/services/gitnexus_indexer
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      WORKSPACE_URL: "${WORKSPACE_URL:?WORKSPACE_URL must be set — SSH URL of the workspace management repo}"
      SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
      GITNEXUS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS: "${GITNEXUS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS:-300}"
      HOME: /gitnexus-data
    volumes:
      - gitnexus-data:/gitnexus-data
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.25"
          memory: 512M

  gitnexus-server:
    build:
      context: ${GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH:?Set GIT_NEXUS_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
        of your git-nexus clone}/services/gitnexus_server
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      HOME: /gitnexus-data
      GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRIES: "${GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRIES:-10}"
      GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRY_DELAY: "${GITNEXUS_STARTUP_RETRY_DELAY:-5.0}"
    ports:
      - "${GITNEXUS_SERVER_PORT:-8002}:8002"
    volumes:
      - gitnexus-data:/gitnexus-data
    depends_on:
      - gitnexus-indexer
    networks:
      - agents-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 1G
        reservations:
          cpus: "0.1"
          memory: 128M

# ── Networks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
networks:
  agents-net:
    # Bridge network shared by the orchestrator, dynamically-spawned executor
    # containers, broker, Redis, and the RAG stack.
    # Executor containers join via --network agents-net in DockerRunAdapter's
    # `docker run -d` call and resolve `broker` by service-name DNS.
    driver: bridge

# ── Volumes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
volumes:
  workspaces-orchestrator1:
    driver: local
  workflow:
    driver: local
  redis_data:
    driver: local
  qdrant_data:
    driver: local
  # PR index cursor state — scoped per project by COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME prefix.
  pr_index_state:
    driver: local
  gitnexus-data:
    driver: local

# Agent Runtime — local-docker Quickstart (decoupled dispatcher topology)

Run orchestrators alongside a standalone dispatcher that spawns executor containers.
The orchestrator is unprivileged — it holds no Docker socket and no credentials.

> **New to local deployment?** Start with [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md) (`local-subprocess` — single container, easier setup). Switch to `local-docker` when you need:
> - The decoupled data flow that mirrors the production architecture
> - Multiple orchestrators sharing work from the same task queue (M:N)
> - Per-task container isolation (executor runs in its own container)
> - Verified concurrent-coexistence testing (bundled ∥ standalone, T7)

---

## How it works

```
┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
│ orchestrator │  │ orchestrator │  ← N orchestrators, each claims tasks
│   agent-1    │  │   agent-2    │    via git push race; enqueues DispatchJob
└──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘    to dispatch stream (no Docker socket)
       │  XADD dispatch   │
       └────────┬─────────┘
                ▼
         Redis (platform:dispatch stream)
                │
         XREADGROUP │ XAUTOCLAIM
                ▼
      ┌──────────────────┐
      │    dispatcher    │  ← holds Docker socket + credentials
      │  (pool of N)     │    per-handle spawn lock (SET NX) → no double-spawn
      └────────┬─────────┘    global cap via GET /registry-size on broker
               │  docker run -d executor:current
               ▼
  ┌─────────┐  ┌─────────┐  ┌─────────┐
  │executor │  │executor │  │executor │  ← one container per task
  │ for T-x │  │ for T-y │  │ for T-z │    logs → stdout (LOG_SINK=none)
  └────┬────┘  └────┬────┘  └────┬────┘
       │  runner wrapper POSTs /callback
       └──────────────┬───────────┘
              ┌───────┴────────┐
              │  broker:7000   │  ← Go broker + Redis (completion queue)
              └───────┬────────┘
                      │ listCompleted()
              ┌───────┴────────┐
              │  orchestrator  │  ← any orchestrator drains (opportunistic M:N)
              └────────────────┘    advances FSM, broker.ack()
```

The orchestrator enqueues a credential-free `DispatchJob`; the dispatcher injects
`GITHUB_TOKEN` + `SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` and spawns the container. Executors write logs
to stdout only (`LOG_SINK=none`; no management-repo git flush on this path).

---

## Prerequisites

Everything from [QUICKSTART.md prerequisites](QUICKSTART.md) plus:

- Docker socket accessible at `/var/run/docker.sock` on the **host** (used by the **dispatcher**, not the orchestrator)
- Docker on the host can pull / has access to the executor image (`executor:current`)
- **`PLATFORM_BIN_DIR`** — absolute host path to `runtime/runner-wrapper/` in your local workflow clone

---

## 1. Configure

Same project-directory setup as `local-subprocess`:

```bash
cd runtime/orchestrator/templates

mkdir -p .projects/my-workspace
cp .projects/.env.example .projects/my-workspace/.env
cp .projects/agent.yaml.example .projects/my-workspace/agent.yaml
```

Edit `.projects/my-workspace/.env` — same required values as `local-subprocess`, plus:

```dotenv
# Switch to the decoupled dispatcher topology
RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker

# Absolute host path to runtime/runner-wrapper/ in your local workflow clone.
# The dispatcher passes this to `docker run -v` so executor containers find runner.js.
# Must be an absolute path — no ~ expansion.
PLATFORM_BIN_DIR=/absolute/path/to/workflow/runtime/runner-wrapper

# Host path for per-handle workspaces. Docker creates exec-<handle>/ subdirs here.
# Default: /tmp/agent-workspaces (uncomment to override)
# DISPATCHER_WORKSPACES_HOST_PATH=/tmp/agent-workspaces
```

`RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker` tells `start.sh` to use `docker-compose.local-docker.yml`
and tells the orchestrator binary to load `QueueDispatchAdapter` (XADD to dispatch stream)
instead of spawning containers directly.

---

## 2. Start

```bash
# Build and start: redis, broker, dispatcher, orchestrator-1, RAG stack
./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d
```

`start.sh` detects `RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-docker` and automatically uses
`docker-compose.local-docker.yml`. The `--build` flag also builds `executor:current`
(the `executor` service, a build-only service that exits immediately after tagging).

To follow logs:
```bash
./start.sh my-workspace logs -f orchestrator-1
./start.sh my-workspace logs -f dispatcher
./start.sh my-workspace logs -f broker
```

---

## 3. Verify

```bash
# All containers running? (should include redis, broker, dispatcher, orchestrator-1,
# qdrant, rag-server, indexer — executor exits immediately after tagging its image)
./start.sh my-workspace ps

# Broker healthy?
curl -s http://localhost:7000/health | jq .

# Registry size (in-flight executor count via broker):
curl -s http://localhost:7000/registry-size | jq .

# Orchestrator using local-docker profile?
./start.sh my-workspace logs orchestrator-1 | grep runtime_profile

# Dispatcher connected to Redis and waiting for jobs?
./start.sh my-workspace logs dispatcher | grep dispatcher_started
```

Expected:
- broker responds `{"status":"ok"}`
- orchestrator logs show `"runtime_profile":"local-docker"`
- dispatcher logs show `"type":"dispatcher_started"`

---

## 4. Concurrent coexistence (bundled ∥ standalone)

To run a bundled (`local-subprocess`) orchestrator alongside the standalone one:

```bash
./start.sh my-workspace up --build --profile concurrent-bundled -d
```

The `concurrent-bundled` profile adds `orchestrator-bundled` (full image with Claude CLI,
`RUNTIME_PROFILE=local-subprocess`) to the stack. It uses a separate named volume for
`WORKSPACES_ROOT` to prevent workspace-dir collisions. Both orchestrators compete for
tasks via the same git push race — no interference. The bundled one executes tasks as
child subprocesses (git log flush active); the standalone one dispatches via the Redis
stream (stdout logs only). Designed for T7 concurrent-coexistence verification.

---

## 5. Stop and reset

```bash
# Stop all containers (keep volumes):
./start.sh my-workspace down

# Stop and wipe volumes (full re-clone + Redis flush on next start):
./start.sh my-workspace down -v
```

---

## Differences from local-subprocess

| | local-subprocess | local-docker |
|---|---|---|
| Executor runs as | child process inside the orchestrator container | separate `docker run -d` container per task |
| Service name | `agent-1`, `agent-2`, `agent-3` | `orchestrator-1` (+ optional `orchestrator-bundled`) |
| Broker | embedded in-process | separate Go service + Redis |
| Dispatcher | none (orchestrator spawns directly) | dedicated `dispatcher` service (Docker socket + creds) |
| Dispatch queue | none | Redis Stream `platform:dispatch` (XREADGROUP/XAUTOCLAIM) |
| LOG_SINK | `git` (management-repo flush) | `none` (stdout only — injected by dispatcher) |
| Orchestrator socket | present (harmless in subprocess mode) | **absent** — orchestrator is unprivileged |
| Concurrency | one task at a time per agent container | up to `DISPATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default 5) across the dispatcher pool |
| Global spawn cap | in-process counter (resets on restart) | broker `GET /registry-size` (shared across all dispatcher instances) |
| Orchestrator image | `orchestrator-bundled` (includes Claude CLI + executor) | `orchestrator` (~500 MB smaller — no bundled Claude CLI) |
| Compose file | `docker-compose.yml` | `docker-compose.local-docker.yml` |

---

## Common issues

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `PLATFORM_BIN_DIR not set` | Set `PLATFORM_BIN_DIR` in your `.env` to the absolute host path of `runtime/runner-wrapper/` |
| Executor container fails with `runner.js not found` | `PLATFORM_BIN_DIR` is wrong — verify the host path exists and is absolute (no `~`) |
| `broker: connection refused` in dispatcher logs | `RUNTIME_PROFILE` not set to `local-docker` in `.env` — check `start.sh` picked `docker-compose.local-docker.yml` |
| `Cannot connect to Docker daemon` in dispatcher logs | Docker socket not accessible — verify `/var/run/docker.sock` is present on the host |
| `nonce_mismatch` in broker logs | A runner retried after the nonce was already consumed — harmless; broker rejects replays by design |
| Executor containers accumulate in `docker ps -a` | The dispatcher's DLQ backstop and broker ack clean up containers; call `docker rm` manually for pre-shutdown orphans |
| `executor_spawn_failed` — image not found | Executor image not yet built — run `./start.sh my-workspace up --build -d` |
| Orchestrator shows `runtime_profile: local-subprocess` | `RUNTIME_PROFILE` not set to `local-docker` — verify with `./start.sh my-workspace logs orchestrator-1 \| grep runtime_profile` |
| Double-spawn / duplicate executor containers | Should not happen — per-handle spawn lock (`SET NX PX`) in dispatcher prevents it. If observed, check dispatcher logs for `spawn_lock_lost` events |
